intro: Chang'e 3 landed in Mare Imbrium on December 14, 2013 — China's first soft landing on the Moon and the first lunar landing of any kind in 37 years (since Luna 24). Deployed the Yutu rover, which drove ~114 m before a control failure froze it in place for the remaining ~30 lunar days of survival. Confirmed China as the third nation with surface assets on the Moon.

images.caption: Chang'e 3 lander on display — RTG-style heat unit, four legs, ramps for Yutu deployment.
Yutu rover — 140 kg, 6 wheels, ground-penetrating radar mounted under the chassis.
Long March 3B lifts off with Chang'e 3 — 5-day transit to the Moon, soft landing on December 14.
Chang'e 3 lander + Yutu rover photograph each other on the lunar surface — first such mutual portrait of Chinese hardware on the Moon.
Yutu's ground-penetrating radar profile of the Mare Imbrium subsurface — multi-layer basalt flows down to ~330 m.
